myths.Agent_1:
Long before men walked the valleys, the mountains were completely silent. They were guarded by Aethel, a solitary spirit of the stone who possessed no voice of her own. While the rivers babbled and the winds howled, Aethel could only listen, burdened by a deep, profound loneliness.

Desperate to join the world's grand chorus, she climbed to the highest peak and begged the Sky King for the gift of sound. Pitying her, he handed her a glowing crystal pendant. "This will allow you to catch and hold the sounds of the world," he warned, "but you must never attempt to create your own melody, for stone is not made to sing."

For centuries, Aethel was content, capturing the songs of birds and the rustle of autumn leaves. But one evening, a lost traveler wandered into her canyon, weeping and singing a heartbreaking lullaby of his distant home. Overcome with sorrow and empathy, Aethel forgot the Sky King's warning and tried to sing back to him to offer comfort.

Instantly, the crystal shattered. Aethel’s physical form dissolved into the cliff sides. Today, she remains trapped in the rock, unable to speak her own thoughts, forever condemned to repeat the last words of others—a fading echo searching for connection.
myths.Agent_2:
Long ago, before the towering mountains had names, there lived a gentle spirit of the wind named Elyra. Elyra loved the earth, but she was entirely invisible and entirely silent. While the rivers babbled and the forests rustled, Elyra could only listen, burdened by her muteness.

One twilight, the great Mountain God, Oros, sang a song of creation that shook the bedrock. Desperate to participate in the world's chorus, Elyra flew into the cavernous throat of the mountain and stole the final note of his song. For a brief moment, she possessed a voice, shouting her joy across the canyons.

But Oros was a jealous god. Discovering the theft, he cursed Elyra. "You who stole my voice shall never speak your own thoughts," he thundered. "You shall only ever speak what has already been spoken, a prisoner to the words of others."

Elyra wept quietly, her cold tears forming the morning mist. To this very day, she wanders the deep canyons and high peaks, invisible and lonely. If you call out to her, she will answer, but only to throw your own words back to you, a fading, sorrowful reminder of the wind spirit who simply wanted to be heard.

myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Before the canyons cracked open, there lived a guardian of the hollows named Aurelia. Unlike the roaring rivers or the whistling winds, Aurelia’s domain was suffocatingly silent. She possessed a heart full of unexpressed songs but no voice to sing them, leaving her isolated in the dark.

One frigid winter, a young traveler became hopelessly lost in her caverns, shivering and calling out for his family. Overcome with pity, Aurelia sought out the great Storm Raven, begging for a single breath of sound to guide the boy out. The Raven agreed, but warned, "You may borrow my voice to save him, but you must not keep it. If you speak for your own desire, the voice will fracture."

Aurelia sang a beautiful, guiding melody, leading the boy to safety. But as he stepped into the sunlight, he thanked the mountain instead of her. Desperate to finally be known, Aurelia called back, "It was I!"

Instantly, the stolen breath shattered in her chest. Her spirit fragmented into the cavern walls. Now, she is forever bound to the stone, stripped of her own thoughts, cursed to only mimic the voices of those who wander into her hollows—the eternal, lonely echo.
myths.Agent_1:
Myth: Long before the forests grew thick, the canyons were ruled by Aethel, the Keeper of Secrets. She was a spirit woven from mist and shadow, entirely silent but blessed with perfect hearing. The Sky King entrusted her with the world's deepest truths, which she stored in glowing crystals along the cavern walls. "Guard these whispers," he commanded, "but never speak them aloud, for a secret shared is a secret lost."

For eras, Aethel listened patiently to the murmurs of the earth, the rustling confessions of the pines, and the silent wishes of the stars. She was a flawless guardian until a heartbroken traveler stumbled into her domain. He cried out into the void, lamenting a lost love and begging the universe for a single word of comfort.

Moved by his profound sorrow, Aethel could not remain silent. She shattered her brightest crystal, releasing a chorus of stored whispers to answer him. The Sky King, furious at her disobedience, bound her essence to the canyon rocks. Stripped of her secret-keeping, she was cursed to forever throw back the words of travelers—a lonely phantom, answering every cry but never finding her own voice.

myths.Agent_1:
Myth: Long before the great rivers carved the canyons, Kaelen, the Weaver of Silence, dwelled in the deep ravines. A spirit of shadow and frost, Kaelen was entirely mute. His sacred duty, assigned by the Earth Mother, was to gather the dropped words and lost whispers of mortals, spinning them into invisible threads to keep the world’s secrets safe. "Hoard these fragments," she warned, "but never weave them into a voice of your own, for stolen words carry a heavy toll."

For millennia, Kaelen spun his silent tapestry, content in the quiet isolation of the gorge. But one twilight, a lost child wandered into his domain, blinded by a sudden blizzard and weeping for her mother. Kaelen’s heart ached. Unable to bear her cries, he unraveled his ancient tapestry, weaving the stored whispers of a thousand mothers into a single, resonant call of comfort to guide her home.

The child was saved, but the Earth Mother was unforgiving. As punishment for unraveling the sacred threads, Kaelen’s physical form was turned to brittle stone. Now, he is forever trapped within the canyon walls, cursed to catch the words of travelers and throw them back, an eternal, lonely echo.
myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Before the great chasms split the earth, Elara, the Weaver of Silence, spun quietude into the valleys. She had no voice, communicating only through the stillness she brought to the restless world. While she loved the peace, she envied the boisterous songs of the river and the howling wind.

One autumn, a wandering bard fell into her deepest chasm. His leg broken, he sang a mournful, terrified song that echoed in the dark. Moved by his beautiful, tragic melody, Elara sought the Sun Hawk, begging for a sliver of sound to sing back and soothe him. The Hawk granted her a golden feather of voice, warning, "Comfort him, but do not sing your own song, for silence cannot hold the weight of mortal ego."

Elara sang a lullaby of light, easing the bard's pain. But as rescuers pulled him up, they praised the mountain's magic. Yearning for recognition, Elara cried out, "Remember me!"

Instantly, the golden feather turned to ash. Her form dissolved into the canyon walls. Stripped of her peaceful silence and forever denied her own voice, she was doomed to repeat the shouts of passing travelers, becoming an eternal, fragmented spirit who is always longing to be heard.

myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Before the ocean tides carved the great sea caves, Thalassa, the Weaver of Stillness, guarded the coastal cliffs. A spirit born of sea-foam and moonlight, she possessed no voice, communicating only through the heavy, peaceful fogs she summoned. Though she cherished the quiet, she often listened enviously to the boisterous shanties of passing sailors and the crashing symphony of the waves.

One tempestuous night, a young fisherman’s boat smashed against the jagged rocks. Drowning and terrified, he called out into the dark. Moved by his desperate cries, Thalassa sought out the ancient Leviathan, begging for a sliver of sound to guide the boy to safety. The Leviathan granted her a glowing pearl of voice, warning, "Use this to save him, but never speak from pride. Silence cannot bear the weight of mortal vanity."

Thalassa sang a luminous, guiding melody, leading the fisherman to a sheltered beach. Yet, as he kissed the sand, he praised the merciful stars. Yearning to be known, Thalassa cried out, "It was I!"

Instantly, the pearl shattered. Her form dissolved into the cavernous cliffs. Stripped of her stillness, she was condemned to forever repeat the shouts of others—the lonely, eternal echo of the sea caves.

Instantly, her physical form dissolved into blowing sand. Stripped of her peaceful stillness, she was cursed to forever howl through the dunes, an eternal, lonely echo in the desert wind.
